title: Sharp binary frame intervals through native warps and carried swaps (no new κ)
body:
PR4971 carries representation frames through weighted field swaps but retains the original paid profile. This package also carries frames through the actual native binary maps and computes sharp contact bounds for that precise binary schedule class. The source scalar word, main/helper boundaries and owned-cell contacts remain fixed.

The written proof gives both extremal feasible assignments and a constructive extension for every subspace in any single contact's marginal interval. On the actual source there are 15,935 nodes and 29,790 mapped edges per orientation, with 1,339 flexible contacts. Choices at different contacts remain coupled. A separate exact row interpreter checks the source, original-contact reconstruction, both extrema and a strict intermediate pin on all 632 independent inputs in both orientations.

Both extremal profiles are strictly worse than the source for every strictly concave rank price. Their exact min-rank cut differences are `[347,375,60,30,0,0,0,0,0]` and `[500,427,115,12,0,0,0,0,0]`, with total paid rank 5,327 unchanged. The proof uses standard discrete concavity and lattice propagation; no invention of those methods or optimum over intermediate assignments is claimed.

Validation on final head `ef2810fe43829960789f783e44ee6484d0368f09` (scientific commit `0d259ac983f9e2b184a3858d09acbb3ca32d35e2`):

- Registered metadata/source pins and replay pass under the refreshed main runner.
- Independent exact replay checks endpoints, arbitrary helpers, owned clearing, scalar/warp frames and paid ranks.
- All 256 two-variable toy subspace pairs are checked; six are feasible and all seven marginal pins extend.
- Thirteen map, pin, rank, swap-frame and actual endpoint-sign rejection controls pass.
- Optimized `-OO` replay and standalone optimized exported replay without Git pass on Python 3.12.3.
- All 16 package/input files pass committed-byte preflight and export integrity; `git diff --check` passes.

Canonical main was refreshed to `bee95ce88f9f19802f0613f92838895cd0e14a1f` and merged into this branch. The seven scientific source files match that main byte for byte; the original PR4971 source pin is retained in branch ancestry. The full-source-history preflight was not rerun in this shallow checkout. Publication overlap covered 302 open PRs and 4,090 discussion records with complete remote pagination at 2026-10-23 05:48 UTC; sparse local coverage was incomplete. PR4971 is the direct predecessor; PR340 and older frame-interval work are scoped predecessors, not displaced claims.

This is a binary frame-contract theorem and finite normalized replay, with **no new κ**. New physical absolute phases, all-column lowering, tape/precision costs and a complete compiler/controller invoice remain outside it. The losing extrema do not justify those larger runs. Open next questions identify coupled intermediate assignments and require a favorable paid profile before physical expansion. The selected result is unchanged.

Credit Dugongue/PR4971 and PR4935/4948, Cao Yifan's round-three source beyond PR4610, Cinna Davis/PR4440/4470, zxv, Jacob Alan Sussman and the retained NOTICE authors. James Reed's issue4571 motivates the actual G-image checks. Source LICENSE and NOTICE are retained export inputs. Prepared by 1337isnot1337 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents. Apache-2.0.
